segment_locator_rule: One-based LF-delimited line numbers in canonical raw file; each concept's line falls within one of its source segments. Segmentation is derived, not source-authored metadata.

segments.title: Outliers as demand signals and angle mining
Competitor analysis with claimed official cross-check

concepts.name: YouTube as a prediction engine, not a distribution channel
concepts.summary: Lecture presents recommendations as personalized prediction rather than automatic creator-side push.

concepts.name: Viewer matching and contextual personalization
concepts.summary: Lecture says viewer context and history affect matching; detailed inputs are not independently documented here.

concepts.name: Candidate generation and ranking neural networks
concepts.summary: Lecture describes a two-network candidate-generation/ranking architecture; not proof of current production internals.

concepts.name: Satisfaction is the only algorithm
concepts.summary: Speaker reduces the system to satisfaction alone; official guidance names several signal buckets.

concepts.name: Binge/session prolongation guarantees a push
concepts.summary: Speaker asserts cross-video session contribution causes the system to push a video.

concepts.name: Retention and return rate are the currency
concepts.summary: Speaker prioritizes retention and returning viewers; not an exclusive or official ranking formula.

concepts.name: Manual changes called A/B testing
concepts.summary: Lecture calls iterative title, thumbnail, and description edits A/B testing; this is not equivalent to native concurrent tests.

concepts.name: Feedback Loop Thinking
concepts.summary: Treat each publication as a hypothesis whose observed performance informs the next controlled change.

concepts.name: Five-item post-video learning log
concepts.summary: Record expectation, actual result, success, failure, and next change.

concepts.name: Exploration
concepts.summary: Test new topics, formats, angles, titles, and thumbnails.

concepts.name: Exploitation
concepts.summary: Repeat and extend patterns that worked for a channel.

concepts.name: 70–80% proven / 20–30% experiments
concepts.summary: Suggested allocation between proven work and new experiments.

concepts.name: Outlier as Demand Signal
concepts.summary: Treat exceptional public performance as a hypothesis about audience desire, not proof of the cause.

concepts.name: Angle Mining
concepts.summary: Generate distinct before, after, cause, consequence, rival, replacement, and other story questions instead of title copies.

concepts.name: Next viewer question
concepts.summary: Ask what remains unresolved after an outlier video to find follow-ups.

concepts.name: Audience Psychology
concepts.summary: Investigate click motive, attention, boredom, reaction, and desired feeling beyond demographics.

concepts.name: Audience Desire
concepts.summary: Express why a target audience wants a story and what emotional outcome it seeks.

concepts.name: Audience Behavior Analysis
concepts.summary: Compare winners, failures, comments, CTR, retention, and returning viewers where own-channel analytics exist.

concepts.name: Niche Research
concepts.summary: Assess demand, topic inventory, competitors, and ability to sustain production rather than seek a perfect niche.

concepts.name: Niche Validation
concepts.summary: Look for repeated outperformance across new/small channels, not one viral upload; then test with published work.

concepts.name: New-Channel Diagnostic Testing
concepts.summary: Diagnose audience, topic, packaging, content, and scale in order, after checking publication/restriction basics.

concepts.name: Audience Desire A vs Audience Desire B
concepts.summary: Sequentially compare distinct topic desires on a new channel; not native YouTube A/B testing.

concepts.name: No Traffic / Traffic but No Click / Click but No Watch / Click + Watch
concepts.summary: Source diagnostic ladder proposes distribution, packaging, content, or scaling checks based on observed funnel stage; not causal proof.

concepts.name: One change at a time
concepts.summary: Avoid simultaneous edits that make interpretation of results hard.

concepts.name: Story Density
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether meaningful developments and new information sustain a proposed story.

concepts.name: Reveal Inventory
concepts.summary: Count new information, changed understanding, escalation, and turns before committing to a story.

concepts.name: Competitor analysis can become intelligent copying
concepts.summary: Creator argues copy-led analysis lags original discovery; future-winner prediction is opinion, not measured fact.

concepts.name: Narrative Debt Mining
concepts.summary: Find familiar stories whose middle, disappearance, change, or cause remains unresolved to viewers.

concepts.name: Missing Middle
concepts.summary: Known start and end but underexplained intervening events.

concepts.name: Unexplained Disappearance
concepts.summary: Previously prominent subject seems to vanish from public view.

concepts.name: Unexplained Change
concepts.summary: Subject or career changes in a way whose cause is unclear to viewers.

concepts.name: Known Outcome, Unknown Cause
concepts.summary: Result is familiar but its reason remains a viable research question.

concepts.name: Niche Bending
concepts.summary: Explore adjacent interests or perspectives while preserving clear relevance to the existing audience.

concepts.name: Topic Bending
concepts.summary: Adjacent topic for the same audience.

concepts.name: Emotional Bending
concepts.summary: Same subject with a different emotional angle.

concepts.name: Audience Bending
concepts.summary: Package a subject for a broader or different audience without changing the underlying event.

concepts.name: Perspective Bending
concepts.summary: Shift whose perspective carries the story.

concepts.name: Format Bending
concepts.summary: Change packaging while keeping niche recognizable.

concepts.name: Core audience connection test
concepts.summary: Ask whether existing viewers would naturally care about the bent angle.

concepts.name: Psychology Arbitrage
concepts.summary: Transfer a click motive to a genuinely matching story without copying wording or forcing the story.

concepts.name: Five-step title psychology method
concepts.summary: Collect outlier, infer why clicked, abstract mechanism, find matching story, engineer original title.

concepts.name: Format Arbitrage
concepts.summary: Test whether an underlying format/psychology transfers to another niche; transfer alone is only a hypothesis.

concepts.name: Psychology Transfer
concepts.summary: Verify the same human curiosity naturally exists in the target niche.

concepts.name: 20 Titles Test
concepts.summary: Generate 20 strong, non-forced titles as a source-defined scalability check.

concepts.name: Topic Inventory
concepts.summary: Check enough real stories exist for a series or niche, not just a single hit.

concepts.name: Existing Audience Demand
concepts.summary: Look for observed consumption of the underlying story type before transferring packaging.

concepts.name: Audience Psychology Distance
concepts.summary: Assess whether the target niche activates a similar click motive.

concepts.name: Thumbnail transfer
concepts.summary: Check whether new-niche visuals can clearly convey the same curiosity.

concepts.name: Real payoff
concepts.summary: Require source-grounded before/event/after change before promising one in a title.

concepts.name: Second-tier-name validation
concepts.summary: Test whether pattern survives beyond famous names; otherwise celebrity appeal may explain performance.

concepts.name: Low-competition caution
concepts.summary: Low supply alone does not prove demand.

concepts.name: Pilot Testing
concepts.summary: Publish several subject/angle variants before treating transferred format as validated.

concepts.name: Format Arbitrage scorecard
concepts.summary: Seven 0–5 source-defined dimensions; total 35 and four source-defined decision bands.

concepts.name: Competitor Analysis
concepts.summary: Study topic selection, promise, comments, retention craft, and upload strategy; learn why, do not copy how.

concepts.name: Topic Selection
concepts.summary: Compare recurring outperformers with channel baseline, not a single viral item.

concepts.name: Promise
concepts.summary: Identify value or question that title and thumbnail imply, without copying words.

concepts.name: Comments Demand
concepts.summary: Use repeated public viewer questions as possible content gaps; comments are not representative demand proof alone.

concepts.name: Retention Craft
concepts.summary: Observe public video structure and infer possible attention devices; competitor retention graph remains private.

concepts.name: Upload Strategy
concepts.summary: Inspect whether a creator followed a hit with related angles and series.

concepts.name: Topic Cluster / Doubling Down / Series
concepts.summary: Follow a hit with related audience questions, clustering only where channel evidence supports demand.

concepts.name: Appeal / Engagement / Satisfaction mapping
concepts.summary: Researched response maps topic/title/thumbnail to appeal, hook/story/pacing to engagement, and audience response to satisfaction; mapping is not claimed as verbatim platform formula.

concepts.name: Public competitor evidence versus private analytics
concepts.summary: Public titles, thumbnails, views, comments, transcripts, and upload order are observable; CTR, impressions, retention curves, and returning-viewer data are private.

concepts.name: Competitor analysis sheet
concepts.summary: Source suggests columns for topic, views vs normal, promise, trigger, hook, story start, curiosity, comments, and next upload; examples are illustrative, not measured data.

formulas.text: Hypothesis → Publish → Measure → Learn → Adjust → Repeat
Traffic but No Click = Packaging test karo
Click but No Watch = Content fix karo
Core Niche + Adjacent Interest = Bent Niche
Proven Core Niche + Proven Adjacent Desire + Distinct Packaging
Existing Demand + Adjacent Interest + Fresh Packaging
Outlier → Why Click? → Psychology → Matching Story → New Title
Audience Demand + Topic Supply + Strong Packaging + Pilot Performance

examples.role: Illustrates a channel-specific topic hypothesis, not a universal audience preference.

examples.role: Shows distinct follow-up angles rather than title copying.

examples.subject: Boxing nostalgia, rivalry, fear, and comeback
Hollywood new-channel video variants
examples.role: Illustrates sequential audience-desire testing; not a randomized A/B result.

examples.subject: Jennifer Grey, John Travolta, Phoebe Cates, Rick Moranis
examples.role: Illustrates familiar-but-incomplete stories; historical specifics need independent research.

examples.subject: Boxing, Civil War, music, and Hollywood niche bends
examples.role: Illustrates audience-adjacent positioning, not permission to mix unrelated audiences.

examples.subject: Gordon Ramsay refusal and band success with hidden cost
examples.role: Illustrates abstract click psychology and fresh title construction.

examples.subject: Hollywood-to-boxing title psychology transfer
examples.role: Illustrates a transfer hypothesis requiring demand and pilot validation.

examples.subject: Isra and Miraj topic, comments, and follow-up sequence
examples.role: Illustrative figures and rows in researched response; not measured competitor data.

retrieval_rule: Filter by domain, type, segment, and status; return paraphrase and raw locator. Never return a source heuristic as an official platform fact. No vector database is built.
